title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: The review identifies four field-level bottlenecks: insufficient in-situ observation of dynamic structural change, immature theory that still misses experiment, unclear and often competitive multifunctional coupling, and a performance–stability trade-off that confines many systems to inert atmospheres.
explanation: Existing methods are said not to capture coordination dissociation and supramolecular reorganization in real time. Theory-directed design remains gapped from targeted synthesis. In multifunctional materials, intermolecular competition and optical–electronic–magnetic interference block simultaneous optimization. Many high-performing systems operate only under harsh inert conditions, limiting devices. Proposed remedies are in-situ diffraction, electron microscopy, and coupled spectroscopies, better models plus machine learning, and cross-scale ligand and surface engineering.
scope: Rare-earth molecule-based functional materials as summarized for 2025, especially dynamic and multifunctional systems intended for devices.
caveats: These are the authors’ field assessment, not measurements from a single comparative study.
